headline: Canadiens’ Suzuki, Dach to return from injuries against Mammoth
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Montreal's Nick Suzuki and Jake Dach are set to return from injuries against Utah, with Suzuki's iron man streak ending after an upper-body injury last month.

Montreal comes back to full strength at 9-3-3 for 21 points, but the underlying picture is less rosy than the record. The Canadiens' share of expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances each side creates) is 48.9 percent so far this season, meaning they have been slightly outchanced overall. At five-on-five it improves to 52 percent, so the gap comes from special teams. Their power play generates 0.49 expected goals per game, and the penalty kill allows 0.85. What has carried them is goaltending: goals saved above expected sits at 5.4, so their netminders have stopped about five more than the chances would predict. Utah is the mirror image. The Mammoth lead the matchup in chance quality at 57.2 percent of expected goals, yet their goalies sit at minus 10.9 saved above expected. Getting Suzuki and Dach back should help Montreal's modest power play, and that is the number we'd watch.
